To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the maximal ST segment/heart ratio is a reliable indicator of the severity of coronary disease before and after coronary bypass grafting.
the maximal ST segment/heart-rate (ST/HR) slope is a reliable index of the presence, severity and the change of coronary artery disease after aorto-coronary bypass surgery.

maximal rate of progression in ST segment depression relative heart rate (ST/HR slope) is a reliable indicator of the number of significantly stenosed coronary arteries and the patency of aortocorornay grafts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assessment of aortocornary bypass grafting by exercise ST segment/ heart rate relation.
the use of the ST segment/heart relation as an index of the presence of coronary heart disease and as a guide to the assessment of aorto-coronary bypass grafting.
the use of the exercise test for the assessment of aortocornary bypass grafting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the maximal ST slope is a valuable tool in the assessment of aortocornary bypass grafting and that it can detect significant disease of the native coronary arteries and/or the bypass grafts.
this new test has been shown to be a reliable and useful tool in assessing the presence, severity, and progress of coronary heart disease.

the maximal ST slope/heart rate relation is a sensitive and specific index of the severity of coronary disease and the adequacy of myocardial blood supply in the individual patient before and after aortocoronay bypass surgery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this test may be used to detect and to assess the degree of coronary heart disease.
the ST/HR slope is an excellent test for the evaluation of coronary artery disease before operation.

the maximal rate of progression ST/HR slope is an accurate index of coronary artery disease, and that the maximal rate progression ST/HR is an accurate index for the detection of the severity of the coronary heart disease in aortocoronay bypass surgery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the maximal ST-HR slope is a reliable index for the assessment of aortocorony bypass grafts.

the maximal ST segment depression/heart rate slope is a sensitive index to assess the patency of aortocorony bypass grafting and to evaluate the severity of coronary artery disease in the bypassed and non bypassed vessels.

the exercise stress test is a very important tool to evaluate patients with known or suspected coronary artery disease, and that it can be used to assess the effectiveness of coronary revascularization.
